title: PRD handshake: owner map, blocker escrow, and acceptance corridor
creator: Maya Fernandez
description:
Goal: Create a durable cross-team handshake for the PRD that maps decision owners, escrowed blockers, and a lightweight acceptance corridor so the runtime, console, and legal teams can sign off without last-minute scope churn. This ticket consolidates outstanding review items, formalizes per-owner remediation SLAs, and defines the acceptance criteria for a gated rollout.

Context: PM draft PRD linked above. Early reviews surfaced three recurring failure modes: (1) ambiguous API surface and contract expectations between console and runtime engineers, (2) unresolved privacy/legal questions around telemetry sampling and retention, and (3) design edge cases for embedded mobile consoles leading to unexpected layout regressions. We need a binding, timeboxed process to resolve these before the canary rollout window (console-2026.04).
acceptance_criteria: All engineering API contract open points resolved and captured in API spec (openapi link) and merged to runtime repo
Design provides final responsive flows for mobile/desktop and hands off assets to eng (figma final frame link), with annotated accessibility and token usage
Legal sign-off on telemetry sampling policy with updated data-flow diagram and KMS handling documented in Confluence
A single rollout matrix exists listing canary percentage, rollback triggers, and metric targets (latency P50/P95, error rate, cost/unit), and SLO-runbook owner assigned
Three blocker categories (P0 architecture, P1 UX, P2 docs/legal) are escrowed with mitigation plans and owner/resolution ETA
decisions: Use API-v2 contract for console <-> runtime (agreed 2026-03-05 retro); eng to implement adapter for v1-compatible customers
Telemetry retention default will be 90 days with optional enterprise override; legal will draft DPA language by 2026-03-10
Design agreed to a simplified mobile header which defers advanced preferences to the desktop console to reduce scope for initial rollout
comments: 2026-03-03 - Maya Fernandez: Collected initial review comments from Eng (ENG-4212) and Design (DES-1103). Creating owner map; asking Legal to prioritize the telemetry diagram update.
2026-03-05 - Ravi Kapoor: Synced with Alex Wu (Runtime) and Priya Nair (Console) — agreed on API-v2 as default contract. Action: Alex to open PR with adapter shim (GH PR link attached).
2026-03-07 - Priya Nair (Design): Uploaded mobile frames and annotated export tokens. Requested clarification on header behavior during offline state. Marked as P1 UX blocker.
2026-03-09 - Legal (Samir Patel): Requested full data-flow sketch showing telemetry path from client -> console -> runtime -> metrics store and KMS usage. Assigned to Eng to provide by 2026-03-11.

2026-03-11 - Alex Wu (Eng): API spec draft posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimetc/pull/1324. Noted a risk: batch window change may add 10-20ms p95 under current autoscaling baseline. Added to SLO heatmap.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Kapoor: Consolidated blocker escrow table and assigned SLAs: P0 48h, P1 5d, P2 10d. Legal thread updated; next cross-team review scheduled 2026-03-15 10:00 PT.
next_steps: Eng: Deliver final API spec and GH PR that includes v1->v2 adapter (owner: Alex Wu) - due 2026-03-11 (in progress)
Design: Confirm final mobile header behavior and provide responsive tokens + export (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2026-03-14
Legal: Draft telemetry DPA snippet and approve retention language (owner: Samir Patel) - due 2026-03-13
PM: Run cross-team decision sync and publish acceptance matrix to Confluence with explicit rollback triggers - due 2026-03-15
notes: Escrow pattern: use a short-lived 'blocker escrow' doc that contains reproducer, impact, mitigation, and owner. If unresolved by SLA, escalate to PM+Eng director for immediate scope trimming.
We will gate the canary start on two hard criteria: Legal diagram sign-off AND Eng PR merged to main with adapter tests passing. Everything else can be phased post-canary as part of staged rollout.
